questions.q: Arrange in increasing boiling point: propan-1-ol, acetone, n-butane, methoxyethane, propanal.
questions.explain: For similar molar mass (58–60), boiling point rises from non-polar alkane (273 K) to weakly polar ether (281 K), to the carbonyls with dipole–dipole forces (322 K and 329 K), to the hydrogen-bonded alcohol (370 K).

questions.q: Among the isomeric amines of formula C₄H₁₁N, which has the lowest boiling point?
options: All three boil at the same temperature
questions.explain: A tertiary amine has no N–H hydrogen for intermolecular hydrogen bonding, so ethyldimethylamine (310.5 K) boils below diethylamine (329.3 K) and n-butylamine (350.8 K).

questions.q: Which statement about the boiling points of C₂ hydrocarbons is correct?
options: Ethane < ethene < ethyne, because polarity increases from ethane to ethyne
Ethene < ethane < ethyne (ethyne sublimes at about −84 °C), and polarity cannot explain the order since all three are non-polar
Ethyne < ethene < ethane, because molar mass decreases
All three have the same boiling point because they are non-polar
questions.explain: The measured values are ethene (−103.7 °C) < ethane (−88.5 °C) < ethyne (sublimes about −84 °C). Explaining it by polarity is the common mistake, since all three are non-polar.

questions.q: o-Nitrophenol can be separated from p-nitrophenol by steam distillation because:
options: o-Nitrophenol forms an intramolecular hydrogen bond, so its molecules do not associate and it is steam volatile
p-Nitrophenol forms intramolecular hydrogen bonds and stays behind
o-Nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonds that make it volatile
o-Nitrophenol has a higher molar mass than p-nitrophenol
questions.explain: In the ortho isomer –OH bonds to the neighbouring –NO₂ inside the same molecule, while p-nitrophenol associates through intermolecular hydrogen bonds and boils much higher.
